UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF INTERIOR
Disturbance of Archeological Resources
There will be no excavation of surface digging of any kind on the demolition sites and hence no potential archeological resources will be disturbed.
Building Clearance in South Boston
There will be no building clearance in South Boston under this program, and hence there is no danger to the Dorchester Heights National Historic Site.
Erosion Control on Cleared Sites
The areas in which abandoned buildings are to be demolished are generally flat, and the specific portions of the sites on which the buildings are located are always flat. In a few cases, (less than 3%) a portion of a site (generally the rear) slopes down to a small gully at a to degree angle. These slopes, which are now overgrown with bushes and weeds, will not be disturbed by the demolition which will occur on the flat portion of the site.
Once a building has been demolished, it will be cleared of rubble and graded. Lots owned by the City of Boston will be eligible for improvements, including grass planting, under the REVIVAL Program (see pg.23 of the EIS). Other lots will soon become overgrown with weeds which, though unattractive, will protect them from erosion.
Sealing Wells and Cisterns
It is unlikely that there are any wells or cisterns in this area, since Boston has had a public water supply since 1796. Now all of the city's water supply originates from the Quabbin Reservoir. If any openings are found during the demolition, they will be sealed by the contractors.
Pigeon Control
The Director of the Boston Housing Inspection Department, who is responsible for pest control in the city, indicates that pigeons are seldom found in or around abandoned buildings in Boston and that they generally do not pose a problem here.
